summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with black tarry stools, dizziness, and hypotension, found to have severe hemorrhagic gastritis and acute on chronic anemia. He was managed with IV pantoprazole, sucralfate, and a temporary hold on warfarin, followed by cautious restart at 2.5 mg daily. Aspirin was discontinued due to recurrent bleeding episodes. An endoscopy confirmed hemorrhagic gastritis, and H. pylori testing was negative. Epistaxis recurred and was treated with silver nitrate cauterization and nasal care. Heart failure was managed with Lasix, and his condition stabilized with improved hemoglobin and euvolemia. He was discharged home with services on pantoprazole, sucralfate, warfarin, iron supplementation, and follow-up plans with cardiology and gastroenterology.
